gaps.sentence: I would never ___ advice from someone I don't respect.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'advice' from the receiver's side
gaps.explanation: take advice from somebody means to accept and follow it; the adviser gives advice.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Stop ___ money on things you never use.
gaps.hint: to use money on useless things; -ing form after 'Stop'
gaps.explanation: waste money on something means to spend it on useless things; 'stop' is followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: We stayed indoors because of the ___ rain.
gaps.explanation: heavy rain is the standard collocation; 'strong rain' is not used.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.
